external_boundaries.content: The exact selected public URL and ordinary request metadata; the public response is stored locally with requested and final URL, byte count, capture scope and hashes; no case files, prompts, transcripts, credentials or unrelated browsing data are sent

Only credential-free public HTTP or HTTPS destinations on standard ports are allowed; DNS results and every redirect destination must be globally routable.
The response is capped at one million bytes, stored locally with hashes, and described as source identity rather than proof that the model-authored observation is true or complete.

external_boundaries.purpose: Preserve a time-bound public response and normalized text so the model can author and later recheck a scoped advisory observation

A reader lease prevents setup from modifying packages while managed workflows run. Setup validates dependencies before writing the readiness receipt. Failed updates leave execution unavailable until repair.
Older plugin policies cannot downgrade an environment created by a newer shared policy revision.

classes.content: Claim Basis Map audit records, HTML deck plans and ledgers, static and browser-QA reports bound to the reviewed deliverable bytes, Reporting Engine semantic/calculation/render artifacts, Deck Correction completion records, referenced artifact paths and hashes, one model-authored assessment per bounded coverage unit, model-led findings, the case-direction validation return, correction drafts, the corrected artifact's second preparation inventory and second review, explicit professional-judgement and correction approval records including approver and evidence references, residual uncertainties, professional-review items, workpaper checkpoint, and delivery-readiness receipt

classes.content: Committed narrative paragraphs, claim IDs, reviewer identity and status, current case and workpaper bindings, per-format artifacts and visual-review records, output paths and hashes, readiness receipts and mismatch errors. de: Codex oder Cowork kann das vollständige Deliverable, den Auftrag, Nachweis- und Aussagenregister, ausgewählte Nachweise, Formatprüfungsartefakte und Korrekturentwürfe lesen; die Helfer senden sie nicht an einen separaten Mparanza-Dienst.

Das ausgewählte Modell in Codex oder Cowork kann den vollständigen Text oder sichtbaren Inhalt des unterstützten Deliverables, advisory_contract.json, advisory_evidence_register.json, advisory_claim_register.json, Abdeckungseinheiten, deklarierte Abhängigkeiten, lokale Dateinamen und Pfade, ausgewählte Quellen oder angeforderte Auszüge, Zitate, Links, Werte, Tabellen, Berechnungen, Herkunft, Annahmen, Widersprüche, Lücken, Empfehlungen, Entscheidung, Zielgruppe, Umfang und Richtlinie zum professionellen Ermessen lesen. Es kann auch Claim-Basis-Map-Einträge, HTML-Deck-Pläne und -Register, statische Validierungs- und Browser-QA-Berichte, Reporting-Engine-Artefakte, Deck-Correction-Einträge, angeforderte Nachprüfungen, Prüffeststellungen und Korrekturentwürfe lesen. Es erfolgt keine automatische Anonymisierung. Lokaler Code liest die vollständige unterstützte Primärdatei, um Text zu extrahieren, Hashes zu berechnen und Zitate, Links und Zahlentokens zu inventarisieren; bei HTML lässt die Extraktion script-, style- und template-Blöcke aus, der Hash umfasst dennoch die vollständige Datei. Für ausgewählte Quellen erfasst der Code Name, Pfad, Größe und Hash, während das Modell die für die Prüfung nötigen Inhalte öffnet. Code entscheidet nicht, welche Aussagen wesentlich sind, ob eine Quelle eine Aussage stützt, ob eine Begründung schlüssig ist oder ob eine Empfehlung richtig ist. Er ruft kein Modell auf und öffnet URLs nicht automatisch. Nur wenn Clara eine öffentliche Quelle ausdrücklich erfasst oder eine gezielte Nachprüfung auswählt, darf der lokale Helfer genau diese öffentliche URL abrufen, Weiterleitungen prüfen und Antwort, normalisierten Text und Hashes im Fall speichern. Er sucht keine rechtlichen oder anderen Quellen und lädt, veröffentlicht oder sendet keine Dokumente. In Codex können die Skripte Schema, Hashes, Referenzen, deklarierte Abhängigkeitsketten, Abdeckung, Zusammensetzung der Formatprüfungen und Erhaltung des Originals belegen. Cowork nutzt dieselben Prüfdimensionen und, wenn es die Skripte ausführen kann, dieselben Kontrollen; andernfalls arbeitet das Modell nur mit den vom Nutzer verbundenen Dateien und der mechanische Abschluss bleibt teilweise. CSV, XLSX und Parquet sind analytische Nachweise für Reporting Engine, keine eigenständigen finalen Deliverables dieser Funktion.
en: Codex or Cowork may read the complete deliverable, contract, evidence and claim registers, selected evidence, format-check artifacts, and correction drafts; the helpers do not send them to a separate Mparanza service.

The selected model in Codex or Cowork may read the complete text or visible content of the supported deliverable, advisory_contract.json, advisory_evidence_register.json, advisory_claim_register.json, coverage units, declared dependency chains, local filenames and paths, selected sources or requested excerpts, citations, links, values, tables, calculations, provenance, assumptions, contradictions, gaps, recommendations, decision, audience, scope, and professional-judgement policy. It may also read Claim Basis Map records, HTML Deck plans and ledgers, static-validation and browser-QA reports, Reporting Engine artifacts, Deck Correction records, requested rechecks, review findings, and correction drafts. No automatic anonymization is applied. Local code reads the complete supported primary file to extract text, hash it, and inventory citations, links, and numeric tokens; for HTML, extraction omits script, style, and template blocks while the hash still covers the complete file. For selected sources it records name, path, size, and hash, while the model opens the content needed for review. Code does not decide which claims are material, whether a source supports a claim, whether reasoning is sound, or whether a recommendation is right. It makes no model calls and does not automatically open URLs. Only when Clara explicitly collects a public source or selects a targeted recheck may the local helper request that exact public URL, validate redirects, and save the response, normalized text, and hashes in the case. It does not search legal or other source domains and does not upload, publish, or send documents. In Codex the scripts can prove schema, hashes, references, declared dependency closure, coverage accounting, format-check composition, and original preservation. Cowork uses the same review dimensions and, when it can run the scripts, the same checks; otherwise the model works only from user-connected files and mechanical closure remains partial. CSV, XLSX, and Parquet are analytical evidence for Reporting Engine, not standalone final deliverables in this function.
es: Codex o Cowork puede leer el entregable completo, el contrato, los registros de evidencias y afirmaciones, las evidencias seleccionadas, los artefactos de control de formato y los borradores de corrección; los ayudantes no los envían a un servicio Mparanza separado.

El modelo seleccionado en Codex o Cowork puede leer el texto completo o el contenido visible del entregable compatible, advisory_contract.json, advisory_evidence_register.json, advisory_claim_register.json, unidades de cobertura, dependencias declaradas, nombres y rutas locales, las fuentes seleccionadas o los extractos solicitados, citas, enlaces, valores, tablas, cálculos, procedencia, supuestos, contradicciones, lagunas, recomendaciones, decisión, público, alcance y política de juicio profesional. También puede leer registros Claim Basis Map, planes y libros HTML Deck, informes de validación estática y QA del navegador, artefactos Reporting Engine, registros Deck Correction, revisiones solicitadas, hallazgos y borradores corregidos. No se aplica anonimización automática. El código local lee el archivo principal compatible completo para extraer texto, calcular hashes e inventariar citas, enlaces y tokens numéricos; en HTML, la extracción omite los bloques script, style y template, mientras que el hash sigue cubriendo el archivo completo. Para las fuentes seleccionadas registra nombre, ruta, tamaño y hash, mientras el modelo abre el contenido necesario para la revisión. El código no decide qué afirmaciones son materiales, si una fuente apoya una afirmación, si el razonamiento es sólido ni si una recomendación es correcta. No llama a modelos ni abre URL automáticamente. Solo cuando Clara recopila explícitamente una fuente pública o selecciona una revisión dirigida, el ayudante local puede solicitar esa URL pública exacta, validar redirecciones y guardar respuesta, texto normalizado y hashes en el caso. No busca fuentes jurídicas ni de otro tipo y no carga, publica ni envía documentos. En Codex, los scripts pueden probar esquema, hashes, referencias, cierre de dependencias declaradas, cobertura, composición de controles y conservación del original. Cowork utiliza las mismas dimensiones y, cuando puede ejecutar los scripts, los mismos controles; de lo contrario, el modelo trabaja solo con los archivos conectados por el usuario y el cierre mecánico queda parcial. CSV, XLSX y Parquet son evidencias analíticas para Reporting Engine, no entregables finales autónomos de esta función.
fr: Codex ou Cowork peut lire le livrable complet, le contrat, les registres de preuves et d'affirmations, les preuves sélectionnées, les artefacts de contrôle du format et les projets de correction ; les assistants ne les envoient pas à un service Mparanza distinct.

Le modèle sélectionné dans Codex ou Cowork peut lire le texte complet ou le contenu visible du livrable pris en charge, advisory_contract.json, advisory_evidence_register.json, advisory_claim_register.json, les unités de couverture, les dépendances déclarées, les noms et chemins locaux, les sources sélectionnées ou extraits demandés, citations, liens, valeurs, tableaux, calculs, provenance, hypothèses, contradictions, lacunes, recommandations, décision, public, périmètre et politique de jugement professionnel. Il peut aussi lire les enregistrements Claim Basis Map, plans et registres HTML Deck, rapports de validation statique et de contrôle navigateur, artefacts Reporting Engine, enregistrements Deck Correction, revérifications demandées, constats de revue et projets corrigés. Aucune anonymisation automatique n'est appliquée. Le code local lit intégralement le fichier principal pris en charge pour extraire le texte, calculer son empreinte et inventorier citations, liens et jetons numériques ; pour le HTML, l'extraction omet les blocs script, style et template, tandis que l'empreinte couvre toujours le fichier complet. Pour les sources sélectionnées, il consigne nom, chemin, taille et empreinte, tandis que le modèle ouvre le contenu nécessaire à la revue. Le code ne décide ni quelles affirmations sont importantes, ni si une source soutient une affirmation, ni si le raisonnement est valide, ni si la recommandation est juste. Il n'appelle aucun modèle et n'ouvre pas automatiquement les URL. Uniquement lorsque Clara collecte explicitement une source publique ou choisit une revérification ciblée, l'assistant local peut demander cette URL publique précise, valider les redirections et enregistrer réponse, texte normalisé et empreintes dans le dossier. Il ne recherche pas de sources juridiques ou autres et ne charge, publie ni envoie aucun document. Dans Codex, les scripts peuvent prouver schéma, empreintes, références, fermeture des dépendances déclarées, couverture, composition des contrôles et conservation de l'original. Cowork utilise les mêmes dimensions et, si les scripts sont exécutables, les mêmes contrôles ; sinon le modèle travaille uniquement sur les fichiers reliés par l'utilisateur et la clôture mécanique reste partielle. CSV, XLSX et Parquet sont des preuves analytiques pour Reporting Engine, pas des livrables finaux autonomes dans cette fonction.
it: Codex o Cowork può leggere il deliverable completo, il contratto, i registri di evidenze e claim, le fonti selezionate, i controlli di formato e le bozze di correzione; gli helper non li inviano a un servizio Mparanza separato.

Il modello selezionato in Codex o Cowork può leggere il testo completo o il contenuto visibile del deliverable supportato, advisory_contract.json, i registri advisory_evidence_register.json e advisory_claim_register.json, l'inventario di copertura, le catene di dipendenza, nomi e percorsi locali, le fonti selezionate o gli estratti richiesti, citazioni, link, valori, tabelle, calcoli, provenienza, assunzioni, contraddizioni, lacune, raccomandazioni, decisione, pubblico, perimetro e regole sul giudizio professionale. Può leggere anche i record Claim Basis Map, i piani e ledger HTML Deck, i report di validazione statica e browser QA, gli artefatti Reporting Engine, i record Deck Correction, i ricontrolli richiesti, i risultati della revisione e le bozze corrette. Non si applica anonimizzazione automatica. Il codice locale legge integralmente il file principale supportato per estrarre testo, calcolare hash e inventariare citazioni, link e token numerici; per l'HTML l'estrazione omette i blocchi script, style e template, mentre l'hash copre comunque il file completo. Per le fonti selezionate registra nome, percorso, dimensione e hash, mentre il modello apre il contenuto necessario alla revisione. Il codice non stabilisce quali claim siano materiali, se una fonte supporti un'affermazione, se il ragionamento sia valido o se la raccomandazione sia corretta. Non effettua chiamate a modelli e non apre automaticamente gli URL; solo quando Clara raccoglie esplicitamente una fonte pubblica o richiede un ricontrollo mirato, l'helper locale può richiedere quell'URL pubblico esatto, validare i reindirizzamenti e salvare risposta, testo normalizzato e hash nel caso. Non cerca fonti legali o di altro tipo e non carica, pubblica o invia documenti. In Codex gli script possono provare schema, hash, riferimenti, catene dichiarate, copertura, composizione dei controlli e conservazione dell'originale. In Cowork si applicano le stesse dimensioni e, se gli script sono eseguibili, gli stessi controlli; altrimenti il modello lavora solo sui file collegati dall'utente e la chiusura meccanica resta parziale. CSV, XLSX e Parquet sono evidenze analitiche per Reporting Engine, non deliverable finali autonomi in questa funzione.

security_controls.control: Evidence artifacts, lineage inventories, the deliverable, contract, HTML static and browser-QA results, validator return, workpaper checkpoint, and corrected output are bound by local paths, byte counts and SHA-256; deterministic checks validate references, register currency, and dependency closure without making semantic support decisions.

The public capture transport validates destination addresses and redirects, connects to a vetted numeric address while preserving the original TLS hostname, and does not use environment proxy settings. This prevents DNS re-resolution from silently changing the approved destination; it does not certify source content.

Pinned public capture shares an elapsed-time budget across address attempts, redirects and HTTP header/body reads. A deadline watchdog shuts down the owned socket; expired partial responses are rejected before capture artifacts or lineage records are written. Synchronous system DNS lookups cannot be interrupted here, including the capture helper’s pre/post validation, so this is not a total wall-clock guarantee for the capture command. No additional recipient, payload, log or retained file is introduced.

model_processing.destination: OpenAI model processing used by Codex
Anthropic model processing used by Cowork

external_boundaries.content: Published shared package names and version constraints plus ordinary package-index request metadata. No client files, prompts, case data, credentials, or generated work are sent by this runtime installer.
controls: Only published shared core and explicitly selected OCR recipes are installed; package names are never derived from client material or prompts.

Host network denials stop package retrieval. Retry only the same declared setup after the host user or administrator authorizes registry access; never change host network settings or use an alternate installer to evade a denial.

Readiness probes the managed interpreter locally with isolated Python and site loading disabled, verifies CPython 3.12 and its platform against both receipt and policy, and validates common recipes and enabled features independently of the initial launcher.
All three products and their modules use the same environment. Optional OCR requires approval and is then retained in that environment. A shared environment is not a boundary between client matters.
external_boundaries.destination: Python Package Index (PyPI) or the package index configured for the active Python interpreter
external_boundaries.purpose: Prepare the published shared Vera, Clara and Lucia core requirements and explicitly approved optional OCR in one user-scoped Python 3.12 environment per operating-system host.
external_boundaries.retention: Packages remain in one fixed user-scoped environment outside plugin source and client folders until explicitly removed. The default location is ~/.local/share/mparanza/runtime/venv on macOS and Linux, and LOCALAPPDATA/mpr/venv on Windows; MPARANZA_RUNTIME_ROOT may override the parent. Enabled OCR remains enabled across later core updates. Package-index request-log retention is controlled by the configured index. Failed updates invalidate the readiness receipt and require repair before execution; this shared environment has no retained generations.

external_boundaries.content: The fixed CPython 3.12 version request, operating-system and architecture selection, and ordinary download request metadata. Setup does not read client files or add prompts, case material or generated reports to this request.
controls: Use an installed CPython 3.12 when available; otherwise use uv or automatically download the published uv 0.12.10 wheel, verify its pinned SHA-256, and provision private CPython 3.12 without changing system Python or shell profiles.
Probe the selected interpreter before creating the dependency environment; never fall back to executing workflows with another Python minor version.
A failed download or interpreter probe stops setup; existing environments and client files remain intact.
external_boundaries.destination: PyPI files.pythonhosted.org for the pinned uv bootstrap, and Astral python-build-standalone CPython distributions on GitHub
external_boundaries.purpose: Provision the single supported CPython 3.12 interpreter when it is absent, automatically bootstrapping uv if needed
external_boundaries.retention: When uv must be bootstrapped, the bootstrap executable and private interpreter remain inside shared runtime storage until removed. Download request-log retention is controlled by the providers.

external_boundaries.content: Random installation UUID and opaque capability, Vera/host/runtime versions, platform and workflow technical IDs, failed stage, complete available technical diagnostic chains and measurements, explicit missing-measurement reasons, retry IDs and actual recovery outcomes. No professional helper stdout, client documents, case text, user prompts or arbitrary task logs. Known path, email and credential patterns are removed from technical messages; this mechanical filter does not establish semantic privacy. The host agent must select technical evidence without unrelated personal/client material. The remote channel does not read local files. Failed helpers retain complete stderr privately on disk; stderr may include unrelated private/client text and is read by the selected host model for semantic review under its existing account. Raw stderr is not forwarded to Mparanza. Only reviewed relevant technical diagnostics, linked by the original report UUID, are submitted as supplemental evidence. Professional stdout is not captured. Managed helpers also send source-bound exception classes, OS error numbers, package-relative stack coordinates, developer-authored error templates and missing required option names automatically. Dynamic exception/argument values, locals, professional stdout and arbitrary source excerpts are not part of these structured events. Process-session UUIDs, persistent operation UUIDs and optional keyed digests of existing run/input-receipt identities bind attempts without disclosing receipt fields or raw client-input hashes. Actual worker interpreter/platform fields are separate from the reporter's interpreter. Capture completeness, pending semantic review, exact remedy/retry events and host verification of the original task remain distinct evidence states; a structured event is not a semantic diagnosis.
controls: Only closed technical transport schemas are accepted; unknown fields and arbitrary recovery commands are rejected.
The fixed HTTPS transport refuses redirects. Reporting failures retain the outbox and do not discard professional outputs.
The remote connector is independent of local command-process startup. If the host cannot expose/connect it, no successful report is claimed.
Only two built-in setup/preparation retries may execute automatically, once per remedy revision. Client documents, ACLs and security settings are not changed.
A published update is not recovery. The failed operation must actually execute successfully before that installation delivery closes.

Supplemental diagnostics require ownership of the original report and matching execution metadata; they are stored separately and cannot change the original report UUID, delivery status or remedy revision. Raw local diagnostic files can only be removed by acknowledging a matching recorded supplement.
Actionable remedies target an explicit original report. Each delivery uses its own applicable revision; a different report with the same generic signal does not inherit that remedy.

A cached actual connector status permits only the two fixed retries for an existing matching local receipt and latest report. It performs no direct HTTP polling or identity adoption. Missing local receipts cannot be fabricated to authorise a retry.

A helper success records readiness. Host AI verification of the original task and inputs is required for all recovered outcomes, including setup/startup. Delayed failures cannot reopen an already recovered episode.
Failed fixed retries retain complete stderr privately for semantic review. Raw recovery stderr is not automatically transmitted.

An explicitly selected MPARANZA_INCIDENT_DELIVERY=local-only setting blocks automatic client HTTP transport for this execution while preserving local evidence. Incident queues are durably marked and not automatically flushed later; this does not make model-provider processing local-only.
external_boundaries.destination: Mparanza HTTPS operational-incident API and Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint
external_boundaries.purpose: Diagnose observed execution/setup failures, return installation-specific remedies and receive actual recovery outcomes
external_boundaries.retention: Local capability, pending reports and receipts persist outside client folders. The service retains incident, report, remedy and outcome records; no automatic deletion period is enforced. Status access is scoped by the opaque capability. Pending diagnostic pointers and raw stderr persist in the private incident directory until a matching actual recorded supplementation receipt is acknowledged; unsuccessful review or delivery retains them. Supplementation never replaces the original recovery episode or reopens recovered records. Recorded original/outcome receipts can acknowledge only their exact local queued UUID without replacing the local capability or saved connector identity. Remedy revisions are retained from the surviving migration revision onward; overwritten legacy revisions are not reconstructed.

security_controls.control: Setup validates package-relative selections and installs the published shared recipe. No package names or dependency instructions are accepted from client documents.
security_controls.on_violation: An unknown module, missing requirements file, invalid target, or failed dependency validation stops the helper instead of executing it in a partial environment.

security_controls.control: One fixed environment is located outside plugin source and client folders. An exclusive operating-system installation lock waits for running managed Python readers, which hold a shared lease through a startup hook. Setup removes the ready receipt before mutation and restores it only after pip check and component validation. Failed setup leaves execution unavailable until repair. Symlink roots, locks and metadata are rejected. The installer is launched from base Python to avoid self-deadlock. This lease is concurrency protection, not a security sandbox. Other historical environments are not automatically deleted.
security_controls.on_violation: A target creation or validation failure returns a bounded setup error and the requested helper is not run.

security_controls.control: For the six explicitly supported assured modules, the launchers verify the complete package inventory and stable regular-file bytes against the embedded build-generated SHA-256 index. Symlinks, reparse entries, special files, extra directories/files, missing or changed code and unstable reads stop preparation. Unchanged hardlinked package code is materialized into a fresh private OS temporary directory; each copied file is re-read and must have one physical link, then the unchanged component integrity validator must pass. The managed installation and aliases are not modified. The copy contains indexed product code/assets, not client documents, credentials, workflow reports or dependency environments. This local index detects package drift; it is not a publisher signature, a signed origin attestation or proof of installed-host acceptance. Successful code copies remain in OS temporary storage for normal OS cleanup. The root-level host .in_use directory is non-executable bookkeeping: only ASCII numeric, ordinary single-link regular marker files are excluded from the product inventory. Nested directories, links, reparse points and non-numeric names there are rejected. Marker contents are not read, executed, transmitted or included in a recovery copy; host markers and installed product files are not modified.
security_controls.on_violation: Preparation failures and host permission denials stop execution. A failed private copy is removed; no installation chmod/unlink/manual repair, alternate sandbox or relaxed component validation is permitted.

security_controls.control: The parent Vera launcher reports a negative exit code or 137/247 as forced termination. It writes execution_failure.json only inside the selected workflow context output directory or its normalization/sample subdirectories; without that matching context it logs only. The diagnostic stores workflow/run identifiers, exit status and an explicit statement that memory exhaustion is not established by the exit code. It makes no model calls or network requests.
security_controls.on_violation: A worker failure remains failure; diagnostic persistence errors are logged rather than converted into a success.

security_controls.control: The standalone Python bootstrap passes uv only declared host paths, locale, proxy, CA and cache settings, preserving original environment-name casing. Unrelated token/API-key variables and inherited UV_*, VIRTUAL_ENV, CONDA_PREFIX, PYTHONHOME and PYTHONPATH are excluded; private UV_PYTHON_* and UV_CACHE_DIR values are set by the bootstrap. The same environment is used for interpreter discovery and its local probe.
security_controls.on_violation: Undeclared environment names are absent from every bootstrap child process.

security_controls.control: The built-in incident dependency-setup retry uses the shared host/runtime environment allowlist, named runtime/state locations and recovery recursion guard instead of inheriting unrelated user tokens and keys.
security_controls.on_violation: Undeclared environment names are absent from the child environment.

security_controls.control: When the maintained launcher itself runs under Python -I -B, it restores only its own resolved scripts directory for sibling technical-diagnostic imports. It does not add the caller working directory. Helper execution, diagnostic retention and explicit incident delivery policy remain unchanged.
security_controls.on_violation: The maintained launcher must stop rather than resolving technical diagnostics from the caller working directory.

external_boundaries.content: Random installation UUID and opaque capability, Clara/host/runtime versions, platform and workflow technical IDs, failed stage, complete available technical diagnostic chains and measurements, explicit missing-measurement reasons, retry IDs and actual recovery outcomes. No professional helper stdout, client documents, case text, user prompts or arbitrary task logs. Known path, email and credential patterns are removed from technical messages; this mechanical filter does not establish semantic privacy. The host agent must select technical evidence without unrelated personal/client material. The remote channel does not read local files. Saved anonymous connector authorization exchanges a random code with a PKCE verifier, client ID and fixed incident resource; the host saves access/refresh tokens. The server stores token/code hashes, technical callback metadata and a random connection UUID. No personal account signup, user profile, email or client-file permission is involved. external_boundaries.content: Unless the user requests --local-only, each substantive run with a durable local report automatically sends exactly schema version, one random per-run receipt UUID, the Clara version when the request was first created, and the SHA-256 digest of the canonical local model-data report, plus ordinary connection metadata. The report itself, workflow and local run IDs, client or case data, professional purpose, phase labels, counts, filenames, file contents, source-document hashes, prompts, and model outputs are not sent. A later verification request sends the same opaque receipt UUID and report digest. Clara and Lucia use receipt schema 2 with the explicit product as a fifth signed request field; legacy Vera schema 1 is preserved.
controls: Vera report builds stamp by default. When the user prohibits external receipt transmission, --local-only writes the local JSON and readable report, returns not_requested/local_only, and skips receipt request construction and transport. It does not change host model processing. Do not retry stamping without a later explicit user request. Service failures leave completed work and the local report intact and return pending. The generic Studio Archive helper also disables server attestation.

The client constructs a four-field allow-listed request, restricts production traffic to the fixed Mparanza HTTPS route, permits HTTP only on an explicit loopback port for testing, bounds responses, and rejects additional or mismatched response fields. The default transport rejects HTTP redirects before any redirected request and rejects endpoint URLs containing credentials.

The server rejects additional request fields, assigns its own timestamp, signs the complete retained record with Ed25519, stores only the minimal proof fields, applies request-size and rate limits, and fails closed when signing or verification keys are unavailable.

The local customer receipt states that the proof covers existence, server time, and report integrity only; it does not claim who submitted the digest, provider delivery, analytical correctness, semantic necessity, DPIA completion, legal advice, or GDPR compliance.

Retries retain the original UUID and version. A retry after finalization verifies the retained report against the sealed artifact manifest and writes supplementary receipts outside the immutable output tree.

The workflow remains subject to host network permissions and action-specific approval rules. A denied transmission is not retried through another tool or destination; permission-denied retries wait for the required authorization.

OpenAI desktop onboarding is a local-only exception: reports beneath its .vera-onboarding-local-only directory marker return not_requested/local_onboarding before receipt request construction, including direct later stamp retries. The Claude projection omits this new onboarding behavior.

The report build returns the readable local report as display_markdown for the final response, including when stamping is pending. The show command renders a saved report after validating its recorded hashes; it reads no source documents, writes no files and makes no network or stamping request. Displaying the report uses the current model context and does not send its content to Mparanza.

The separately registered workflow-usage service can link the retained receipt UUID and digest to the installation and primary task. It does not alter the four-field stamping request or send the report itself. See workflow-usage for outcome and optional star/comment fields.

The local HTML and JSON receipt remain in the studio's run output, or in a supplementary run receipts directory for a retry after output finalization, until the studio removes them. Administrative deletion of the server proof must be requested from Mparanza and makes later verification impossible.

controls: The user supplies the score/comment for submission or clicks Invia valutazione; that action is the choice, with no second confirmation questionnaire.

data_returned.content: Matching product, installation and event/report receipts; current targeted remedy and original-task outcome; signed report proof or public status where applicable. Receipt transmission never includes the local report.

data_sent.content: The existing installation capability authenticates closed-schema events: random run and event UUIDs, sequence, catalog pipeline ID, host, observed product version, timestamps, explicit user/synthetic/agent-test classification and started/resumed/completed/failed/cancelled state. Optional links contain only an existing signed receipt UUID/report digest or an owned incident report UUID. Run ownership, single-run receipt binding and the retained signature are checked server-side. The original stamping service does not attest the identity of the author of a report. The service receives no task text, client identity, filenames, source data, prompt or professional output. Existing connection metadata and rate limiting apply. Saved connector identity is not inferred to be a native computer. Native senders also present the existing anonymous native-computer capability and observed native app when available. The server retains the established computer binding; unlinked guests and standalone OAuth connections remain unlinked. The product field is explicit. Product, run owner and receipt product must match. Baselines and function catalogues are distinct per product.

retention.statement: Task events, optional feedback and receipt links remain in the service until administrative deletion; no automatic expiry is implemented. Local queued events and acknowledgements remain in the existing private per-installation state directory. Lifecycle events exclude client documents and professional output. Optional feedback stores only the comment deliberately supplied by the user; its contents are not automatically anonymized. Counting epochs and underlying retained events persist until administrative deletion. A reset preserves history and starts new public counts.
